preview: Software Development Analyst Intern interview experience at Citi detailing online test, technical round, and HR round.
content: CITI GROUP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE (INTERNSHIP) ROLE:Software Development Analyst Intern Utkarsh Chheda TY IT PPT:- The PPT was conducted on 6th September.Do attend the PPT as it is crucial when you are asked company specific questions.Make note of important points.The PPT contains info about the company’s values,reach,goals,employee commitments,internship program details and much more. ROUNDS:- 1) Online Test - 11th September(9:00 PM to 11:00PM) 2) Technical Interview - 14th September(11:00AM to 11:20AM) 3) HR interview - 14th September(11:40AM to 12:10PM) ROUND 1 : ONLINE TEST:- Criteria: CPI 6+ and no active backlogs.The test could be given by students of all departments. The Test was conducted on AMCAT platform The Test consisted of 5 sections. There were sectional timers. You cannot switch between sections. Also you cannot navigate through the questions within a section. There was no negative marking. General tip: Be fast in solving these questions as time becomes a crucial factor for elimination. 1. CS subjects’ based MCQs (25 Questions in 35 minutes) 1 MCQs are based on stacks, queues, trees, searching, sorting techniques, output prediction,basic programming questions,OOPS,debugging etc.In my test,I found high emphasis on sorting,queues and output prediction. Your basics should be really clear for this.You must have the ability to trace algorithms quickly because questions could be on a specific section of an algorithm rather than the final output.Eg. the kth iteration in selection sort. 2. Aptitude (16 Questions in 16 minutes) MCQs on topics like work and time, probability, permutations and combinations, percentages, ages, profit and loss, etc. 3. Logical Reasoning (14 Questions in 14 minutes) Questions on pattern completion,human relationships,puzzles on encoding of letters,puzzles like A comes before G and H comes before B etc.. 4. Verbal Reasoning (22 Questions in 18 minutes) Antonyms, synonyms,logical ordering of sentences and passages etc. The questions were easy. There were two passages. Each passage had around 3-4 questions. In each passage one question was based on the summary of the passage and what the author is trying to convey.So reading the passage carefully and patiently once helps a lot and saves time. 2 5. Coding section (2 Questions in 60 minutes) a. Consecutive Gray Code Numbers. A gray code sequence is one in which two successive terms differ by only one bit. Print 1 if binary representation of given numbers can be placed successively in a gray code sequence else print 0. Example: ●areGrayNeighbors(9,11) --> 1 (since (1001, 1011) differ in only one bit and are neighbors) ●areGrayNeighbors(9,10) --> 0 (since (1001, 1010) differ in two bits) ●areGrayNeighbors(14,10) --> 1 (since (1110, 1010) differ in only one bit and are neighbors) If you want to know whether two Gray codes a and b are neighbors, you have to check whether previous(a) = b OR next(a) = b. For a given Gray code, you get one neighbor by flipping the rightmost bit and the other neighbor bit by flipping the bit at the left of the rightmost set bit. For the Gray code 1010, the neighbors are 1011 and 1110. In the question the definition of successive terms and neighbors wasn’t explicitly mentioned. Passed 25/25 test cases b. Maximum Toll Revenue There are N cities with unique city codes from 1 to N and are connected by N-1 roads.The road network is in the form of a tree which connects two cities.A path is a road,combination of roads,connecting two cities.Each road has a toll booth that collects toll equal to maximum number of paths of which that particular road is a part.We need to identify the road which 3 collects maximum toll revenue(output is pair of cities connected by road).If two or more toll booths collect same total revenue,then we have to print the pair of cities with lexicographically smaller city codes. The inputs to the tree were taken like a graph (adjacency list) unlike a node based tree.The way of taking input did confuse a lot of people,this had also happened in a previous test. I cleared 4/13 test cases for this question. 76 students were shortlisted for the interviews ROUND 2 : TECHNICAL INTERVIEW:- The interviewer was really friendly and he began the interview by introducing himself. Then he asked the standard “Tell me about yourself” question.I talked about my skills,my projects and extracurriculars.. He had my resume and asked me about the language I was proficient in.I mentioned C++.My resume also had a mention of Python,so he asked me about why I preferred C++ over python and what all things I had done in Python.Then he shifted his focus on the projects mentioned in my resume. I had mentioned 3 web development projects.All of them were developed using the MEN stack.He asked me to show the code of the project and the part where I had contributed as it was a team project.He also asked me to start my local server and show my project to him.Since I had worked on the backend side of the project,he asked me about GET requests,EJS templating,MongoDB ATLAS(fully managed cloud database).One of the projects also used QGIS,so he asked about that and how I incorporated that in my project.He also asked whether I knew any front end frontend frameworks. 4 Afterwards I was asked which all data structures I knew.Then I was told to define a data structure and cite differences between an array and a linked list.Moreover I was told to write a code for printing till the nth fibonacci numbers.He asked me to write the code on a editor of my choice.I chose VSCode and was also told to show the output.At first I only give the recursive approach and then asked him about optimizing it via dynamic programming to which he replied that it wasn’t needed.At the end he asked whether I had any questions for him (Always ask questions! It shows your interest in the company)I asked for more clarity on the role of a summer intern and the technologies I would be using in that period. The interview lasted about 20mins of the allotted time of half an hour..I was anxious about my selection for the next round because of this.As the tech interviews were being conducted simultaneously people were being shortlisted for the second round as well. About 30-35 students were shortlisted for the HR round. ROUND 3 : HR INTERVIEW:- When I joined the meet,the interviewer was filling up some records on his other pc.He politely asked me to wait for some time.Then he introduced himself,his role in the Investment Banking Division of CITI and the kind of work they do in that sector.Then he asked me to tell me something about myself.He seemed quite impressed with my intro.I mentioned that I loved trekking and on hearing this he had a huge smile on his face.He asked about which all treks I have been on.I mentioned the Sahyadris and the Himachal treks I have been on and the one which I found the most challenging.He asked me to differentiate between the two kinds of treks and how to prepare for longer treks.He asked me about a few equipments 5 used.He also asked that what propels me to trek and what all things I have learnt while being on one.Moreover,he said that there are a lot of places to explore near his workplace and how refreshing it is to go on a trek in the weekend. Furthermore,he asked me why do I want to join CITI and what do I know about CITI.I replied with a lot of numbers which were shown during the ppt,the global influence and the company’s values and commitment towards its employees.I was asked about how I would work in a global team and collaborate with people.Moreover,he asked me about the challenges I encountered while working on a project and how I worked as a team leader to resolve that issue.Then he asked me whether I had any questions for him(always ask questions,this shows that you are interested to work there). Then he mentioned that you are a nice fit to the company and he would surely recommend my name for the next round.(My joy knew no bounds as I was really not expecting to hear this as interviewers don't usually say that.)I thanked him for that and said that it didn’t really feel like an interview.To this he replied that he had a wonderful time having an interaction with me.With this the HR round concluded. I was wondering about the next round as we were told that there would be only 2 interview rounds.I anxiously waited the entire day for the results.Finally at 10pm,the results were announced and I was one of the 15 students shortlisted for the internship program. ADVICE:- ●Always read company archives on gfg and coc drive(and practice questions company wise as well). 6 ●Give mock interviews (on interviewbit or among your friends).This really helps as it can give you a better insight on your preparation. ●Be well versed with each square centimeter of your resume.You can be asked anything about what you have mentioned.(In one of the past interview experiences,I read that the person had written about Discrete Mathematics in the cv and was asked about Hamiltonian circuits.💀 ●While explaining your project,use the STAR method.STAR(Situation, Task, Action,Result).It gives a proper flow while explaining and you won’t miss out on crucial points. ●Do not lie in your resume,the interviews are smart enough to catch one.Be completely honest of whatever skills you possess. ●Do not take HR round lightly. Prepare for it too.Read the most commonly asked HR questions.Many candidates are eliminated in that round. ●Reading these past experiences has given me invaluable insights about the process and the kind of questions asked.For instance,I got an almost same question in one of the coding rounds.Moreover,many companies do repeat the questions asked in the online test.(Reading past experiences gives an upper edge)😏 ●I was asked a lot about the projects mentioned in my resume.In all interviews,more than 60% of the time was spent on discussing about the projects.Questions like describe the architecture used in your project,write the Mongo schema of your database,write get and post requests,routing,api calls,middleware etc..Though I had an idea about them,but in the months prior to the interviews,I was solely focussing on DSA. ●Give importance to CS subjects like OS,DBMS,CN(not often asked for internships). 7 ●Before the interviews,there was a sheet sent via mail which specifies your interview time and interviewer name(not all mention this).Take advantage of this.I would check their Linkedin profiles and the role and the work they do.This gives an insight on what I should focus more on. ●Do good research about their company.Attend the PPT and keep note of imp points.Know about the company’s CEO and its values. ●Find seniors and friends whom you can confide in.They have been one of the most crucial factors in clearing this interview. ●Always explain your logic and make very sure that you have completely understood what the interviewer is asking, speak out loud, tell the interviewer your approach and then code.Think Loudly!! ●Always start first with the naive approach and then build your solution to an optimized approach.Communicate with your interviewer at all steps.Don't have too long silent phases in the interview.Express your ideas.Catch hints given by the interviewer. ●Don’t just straight away answer the question.Think for a moment before finally answering. ●In internship interviews a lot of candidates are asked puzzles to check one’s logical skills.I would try to solve 3-4 puzzles on gfg each day. ●Based on constraints given, brute force solution can also prove to be sufficient to pass all test cases. Do try brute force solution. ●If not able to think of any sort of solution,try hard coding the outputs.You can probably pass a few test cases just by this.If its a tough question,where others would just give up,this really helps(it helped in my case).One of my seniors suggested this. ●Have good grip over STL(if using c++). ●Don't lose faith in yourself if you get rejected, i was rejected in HILTI and VISA interviews.Analyze what you think could be a possible 8 reason for the same.Take this as an experience which will definitely come to your aid when you finally clear ‘THE Interview’. ●Stay hydrated,and have a good sleep before the imp day.A fresh mind can do wonders. ●Remember ‘LUCK’ is a crucial factor.You need hard work ,dedication ,patience and luck to clear interviews.The process can be unfair at times but it is what it is.Don’t let such thoughts deter your prep. ●There may be times when you will feel dejected,but trust the process,have faith and confidence in yourself.I know it can be very tiring and stressful when you get rejected from interviews or fail to clear the test round.I have been through that.But have faith in your preparation,start afresh and continue to put in your best efforts. ●Internship is not the only thing.Don’t be too harsh on yourself.It’s never too late to begin. OOPS real world I followed Prof Abdul Bari’s course on c++ which had oops. DBMS: DBMS Gate Smashers Playlist Database Indexing Normalization SQL practice on leetcode Quick Revision CN: 10 As far as internships are concerned they don't ask CN questions generally, but you can be prepared with the basics What happens when you type a URL in the browser and press enter?
